raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this season. I'm not a grain farmer — those 4.5 mu are all vegetables, and vegetables are a different game. More cash in, more cash out, more work. Just me and the wife, so labor is tight. Let me go through each field.

---

**My reasoning (as the farmer):**

Our main rotation is cabbage and eggplant on the best two plots — about 2 mu. Eggplant goes in after Qingming when the frost is done, transplants I buy from the market in Quzhou town, around 500 plants per mu. That field runs through October, then I can't fit a full cabbage crop behind it — the timing is too tight. So I do the cabbage-eggplant rotation across years: this year's eggplant field becomes next year's spring cabbage field. The *other* main plot is in fall cabbage, transplanted in early August, harvested by early December.

Extension station people always tell us to do soil testing, I did it once maybe five years back, didn't bother since. I know what my fields need. Eggplant and chili are hungry — I put down 3-4 cart-loads of chicken manure per mu before planting, then compound fertilizer (那个15-15-15的) about 40 kg per mu as base, and I topdress urea every two weeks once the fruit is setting. My neighbor老王 tried reducing fertilizer last year on eggplant and his yield dropped bad, so I'm not cutting back.

Cauliflower gets similar treatment to cabbage but a bit more nitrogen — it's fussier. Chili is the most profitable per mu but the most work and the most pesticide. Aphids and the whiteflies, if I don't spray I lose the crop. Kidney bean is easy — it fixes its own nitrogen, I barely fertilize it, mostly for rotation and to sell at the village market. Spinach goes in after I clear the kidney bean in late summer, gives me a winter crop to sell when nothing else is coming off the field.

Water — the well is 20 meters deep, electric pump. Vegetables I irrigate a lot compared to wheat-maize guys, maybe 8-12 times for eggplant through the summer, furrow irrigation between the rows. Electricity cost adds up but you can't skimp.

Pesticide I buy from the agro-shop on the main road. I read the labels — middle school was enough for that — and I follow the extension station's recommended products when they post them. But I decide how much based on what I see in the field.

Total outlay this year will be around 8,000-9,000 yuan for the whole farm. If the eggplant and chili prices hold up like last autumn we'll clear 25,000-30,000 net. If prices crash like 2024 spring cabbage — well, that's why we spread across six crops.
